Tornado prediction accuracy

Out-of-sample results for the served HazardPulse tornado model, tornado_v3-05a06c843c87. Every number on this page is read from the results files of a pre-registered programme whose final test (every storm of 2025) was run once, after every choice was frozen.

The served model

Modeltornado_v3-05a06c843c87
ForecastsP(a tornado from THIS storm within 60 min); inputs include NWS warning state
Eventa tornado report starts within 10 km of THIS storm's tracked polygon within 60 min
Inputs (30)28 ProbSevere storm attributes, 2 NWS tornado-warning state
Model formLightGBM, 339 trees, scored in NumPy from a JSON payload
CalibrationPlatt on leave-one-year-out scores; Venn–Abers band per storm
Training2020-10-15..2024-12-31, fixed rounds chosen by early stopping on validation 2023
Final test2025, read once: 1,469,977 storm observations, 1,579 tornadic

Protocol: docs/TORNADO_MODEL_PROGRAM.md. Every choice (inputs, model family, hyperparameters, calibration, label) was made on 2023; 2024 was a development test; the model was then refitted on 2020–2024 and scored once on 2025. A forecast is scored against SPC storm reports matched to the storm’s own tracked radar polygon.

Against NOAA and the NWS, on the same storms

  • NOAA ProbTor scores 0.879 as issued and 0.939 with its integer ties broken; the model is +0.031 [+0.022, +0.042] AUC above the tie-broken version, paired by day over 365 days; Brier −0.000036 [−0.000055, −0.000021]. The issued product is an integer percent and 0 for most storms, so its ties are broken by ProbSevere’s own severe probability for a fair ranking comparison.
  • NWS tornado warnings: At the NWS warnings’ own false-alarm rate it catches 30.5% of tornadic storm observations vs the warnings’ 22.7% (+7.7 [+3.8, +10.1] points, using the warning state as an input); without that input it catches 27.5% (+4.7 [−0.2, +8.5] points). The false-alarm rate is the warnings’ own (0.090% of non-tornadic storm observations). A model that reads the warning state measures what it adds on top of the warnings; the figure without that input is the contest on its own.
  • Our previous model (v2): +0.007 [+0.003, +0.010] AUC on the same storms and the same event.

Tested and not served

Each was measured on 2023 under the same protocol. None improved the forecast, so none is in the served model.

  • The HRRR environment at the storm, timed as it is available live: +0.0001 validation AUC (difference of two validation runs).
  • The coherence field (80 km) on top of those HRRR fields: −0.0011 [−0.0032, +0.0007] validation AUC (paired by day; measured before amendment 8 corrected the HRRR timing, which both arms shared).
  • The coherence PDE solution against a Gaussian-smoothing control (9 km): +0.0004 [−0.0008, +0.0015] validation AUC (paired by day; measured before amendment 8 corrected the HRRR timing, which both arms shared).

What makes this different

  • Pre-registered and read once

    Every modelling choice was fixed on 2023 and checked on 2024 before 2025 was scored, once. The protocol and its dated amendments are public, including the ones that corrected our own earlier numbers.

  • Scored against NOAA on the same storms

    The comparison with NOAA ProbTor and the NWS warnings uses the same storm observations, the same event and intervals paired by day.

  • Open and reproducible

    The served model is a JSON file in the repository, scored in pure NumPy; its identity is the hash of its bytes, and every live forecast is appended to a hash-chained ledger.

  • We publish what did not work

    The HRRR environment and the coherence field were tested and did not improve the forecast; the measurements are above.
